Direction is changing, confirmation with Jack Heart pending: "we should lean towards just assuming a server and then making that fast and easy and if it's not faster than not having a server, then that's performance work for us to do". Likely shape: every eval group runs on one Etude-owned eval server per machine that hosts light game processes and owns concurrency; the author's serve (batching) is optional inside it. Until confirmed, do not build further on a separate no-server worker-pool path; work on the parts this does not change (failed retry flag, renting gate by estimated time, thread budgets, scratch and receipts directories, per-match delivery).
